incidents.cause: Both glider pilots' inability to see and avoid the other resulting in a mid-air collision.
The pilot's misjudged distance and altitude while on final approach to land. A factor contributing to the accident was a downdraft.
The pilot's failure to maintain clearance with the rotating rotor blades after he exited the helicopter after landing.
A loss of control during the precautionary landing, which resulted in inadvertent contact between the main rotor and the tailboom. Contributing to the accident was the overloaded condition.

The flight instructor’s delayed remedial action and inadequate supervision during a practice autorotation, which resulted in a failure to maintain adequate main rotor rpm. Contributing to the accident was the wet landing surface.
A loss of engine power due to a failure of the magnetos as a result of inadequate maintenance.
The airplane's impact by a bird during the initial climb.

A total loss of engine power as a result of fuel starvation due to contamination from a thermoplastic polymer used in the fuel system. Contributing to the accident was the pilot’s failure to report debris observed in the fuel system during previous preflight inspections to maintenance personnel.
